title: January 2026 Protests: Alireza Sepahi Executed
content:
According to HRANA, Alireza Sepahi has been executed.

Shahrzad Shahbazi, an attorney, announced in a post that at dawn today, Monday, October 5, the death sentence of Alireza Sepahi, one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests and a defendant in the case known as the “Isfahan Alikhani Square” case, was carried out at Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan.

Yesterday, HRANA reported that Mr. Sepahi had been transferred to solitary confinement and that his family had been summoned for a final visit with him.

It is also worth noting that yesterday, attorney Amirsalar Davoudi announced the marriage of the two prisoners by posting an audio recording of the marriage ceremony of Alireza Sepahi and Mahshad Kashani on his page.

HRANA had previously reported that after the Supreme Court approved a retrial in Alireza Sepahi’s case, his case was referred for reconsideration to a parallel branch of Branch 2 of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court. However, that branch rejected the retrial request without holding a hearing and sent the case to the Enforcement of Judgments Branch for implementation of the death sentence.
snippet: According to HRANA, Alireza Sepahi has been executed.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Alireza Rashidi, a 16-Year-Old Teenager, Arrested by Security Forces
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kolbar News, Alireza Rashidi was arrested.

According to the report, the 16-year-old was arrested by security forces on Wednesday, September 30, in connection with his participation in the protests of January 2026.

As of the time of this report, no information is available regarding the teenager’s place of detention or the charges brought against him.

Background on January 2026 Protests:

It should be noted that protests and strikes by shopkeepers and bazaar merchants began in Tehran on Sunday, December 28, 2025, and within two days spread beyond markets and commercial centers. With the participation of students, citizens, and various social groups, these protests became one of the largest protest movements of recent years. Following the crackdown by security and law enforcement forces, thousands were killed or injured, and tens of thousands were arrested or summoned by security agencies. For more information, readers may refer to HRANA’s comprehensive report titled “Crimson Winter,” documenting the first fifty days following the outbreak of Iran’s nationwide protests.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kolbar News, Alireza Rashidi was arrested.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January 2026 Protests: Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi Executed
content:
According to HRANA, citing Mizan, Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi, son of Khodamorad, was executed.

The Judiciary’s Media Center announced today, October 3, that this citizen allegedly opened fire on security forces using a firearm on January 8, 2026, during protests on Naser Khosrow Street in Shahrekord. He was arrested two days later, and several additional firearms were reportedly discovered in his possession.

According to the institution’s claims, Mr. Jamshidi Kheirabadi also used social media during the January’s protests to “organize and carry out actions against national security.”

The report further alleged that Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi had prior criminal records and judicial cases, including one involving possession of an unauthorized firearm.

Ultimately, Mr. Jamshidi Kheirabadi was sentenced to death on charges of “moharebeh through drawing and firing a firearm” and “assembly and collusion against national security.” The sentence was carried out after being upheld by the Supreme Court.

The report did not specify the date or location where his execution was carried out.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Mizan, Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi, son of Khodamorad, was executed.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Actress Elnaz Shakerdoost Sentenced to One Year in Prison and Additional Punishments for Supporting Protests
content:
According to HRANA, citing Emtedad, the conviction of film and television actress Elnaz Shakerdoost has been upheld on appeal.

Houshang Pourbabayi, an attorney, provided details about the case, stating that Shakerdoost had previously been sentenced by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court to one year in prison on the charge of “propaganda against the regime” for supporting the January protests. As an additional punishment, she was also banned from political, online, and artistic activities for two years. According to Pourbabayi, the ruling was recently upheld in full by Branch 36 of the Tehran Province Court of Appeals.

Regarding the basis for the charges against Ms. Shakerdoost, her attorney added: “My client was sentenced solely for posting a story on her personal social media account following the events of last January, which left every Iranian grieving. From beginning to end, the post was nothing more than a sincere expression of sorrow over the deaths of young people in this country.”
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Emtedad, the conviction of film and television actress Elnaz Shakerdoost has been upheld on appeal.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Execution of Five Prisoners in Arak, Zanjan, and Meshgin Shahr Prisons
content:
According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, at dawn on Wednesday, September 30, a prisoner was executed in Arak Prison.

The prisoner has been identified as Abbas Amirgheshlaghi, 27, and unmarried.

Mr. Amirgheshlaghi was reportedly arrested approximately three years ago on charges related to drug offenses and was subsequently sentenced to death by the Revolutionary Court.

Zanjan Prison: Three Prisoners Executed

According to Iran Human Rights Organization, the three prisoners, who had been sentenced to death in separate cases, were hanged at dawn on Sunday, September 27, in Zanjan Prison.

They have been identified as Fateh Shafiei, 33, a resident of Zanjan and father of one; Hassan Mahdipour, 30, from Mianeh; and Aref Dorosti, 51, from Karaj and father of three.

According to the report, Mr. Shafiei and Mr. Dorosti were arrested approximately three years ago, while Mr. Mahdipour was arrested approximately two years ago, all on charges related to drug offenses. They were subsequently sentenced to death by the Revolutionary Court.

Report on the Execution of a Prisoner in Meshgin Shahr Prison
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, at dawn on Wednesday, September 30, a prisoner was executed in Arak Prison.

title: Mehdi Abiyat Arrested by Security Forces in Ahvaz
content:
According to information received by HRANA, Mehdi Abiyat, 31, was arrested on the evening of Thursday, October 1, by Ministry of Intelligence agents on a street in the Kuy-e Shahrak neighborhood of Ahvaz, without the presentation of a judicial warrant.

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for his arrest, his place of detention, or the charges brought against him.

Mehdi Abiyat, also known as Abu Farouq, is a resident of the Kuy-e Shahrak neighborhood of Ahvaz. Prior to his arrest, he made a living by selling clothes as a street vendor.

title: Three Detainees from January 2026 Protests Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, three citizens arrested during the January 2026 protests have been sentenced to death.

According to information received by HRANA, Khosrow Mohammadiniya, Masoud Tushmalani, and Sirvan Shabani were sentenced to death in a joint case by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. The charges brought against the three citizens in this case include “moharebeh (enmity against God), assembly and collusion with the intent to disrupt national security, and operational activities in support of hostile governments.” The ruling was issued with the signatures of Judge Karimi and Judge Taghizadeh.

The three citizens, who are from Kermanshah, were arrested by security forces on a street in Eslamshahr during the nationwide protests in January 2026.

Following his initial arrest, Masoud Tushmalani was released on bail for a period of time, but was rearrested by security forces several days later.
snippet: According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, three citizens arrested during the January 2026 protests have been sentenced to death.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January 2026 Protests: Mehdi Nami Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Mehdi Nami has been sentenced to death.

According to information received by HRANA, Mr. Nami was recently sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court on the charge of “taking operational action in favor of hostile states.”

Mehdi Nami was arrested by security forces at his home in Tehran in January 2026 in connection with the nationwide protests. He is currently being held at Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

HRANA is reviewing further information regarding the specific acts underlying the charge brought against Mr. Nami in this case.

title: Monthly Report – September 2026: Human Rights Situation in Iran
content:
Executions

During September, at least 59 prisoners, including four women, one juvenile offender, and four Afghan nationals, were executed by hanging in prisons across Iran.

Of those executed, 29 had been sentenced to death on murder charges, 26 on drug-related charges, and one on a charge of rape.

In addition, three individuals were executed on political and security-related charges: Ali Hemmati and Majid Nikandish were executed in Mashhad in connection with the nationwide protests of January 2026, while Hossein Pedaran was executed on charges of espionage and intelligence cooperation with Israel.

During the same month, Iran’s judicial authorities also issued 23 death sentences. Three of those sentenced to death are women, including Mahboubeh Shabani, who was sentenced to death in connection with the January 2026 protests.

Also during the month, Iran’s Supreme Court upheld ten death sentences.

title: Report on the Arrest of Asad Halafi by IRGC Intelligence in Ahvaz
content:
According to HRANA, Asad Halafi, a resident of Ahvaz, was arrested on Saturday, September 26, 2026.

According to information received by HRANA, at around 4:00 a.m., IRGC Intelligence forces went to Halafi’s home in Ahvaz and arrested him. During the arrest, agents also searched his home and confiscated some of his personal belongings.

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for his arrest, his place of detention, or the charges brought against him.

Asad Halafi is 37 years old, married, and the father of two children.

title: Report on the Execution of Seven Death Sentences
content:
According to HRANA, citing Javan Online, at dawn yesterday, Wednesday, September 30, five prisoners at Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj, who had been sentenced to death in separate cases on murder charges, were executed by hanging.

According to the report, one of the prisoners went to his wife’s workplace in August-September 2020 due to a dispute with her and physically assaulted her. Later, when his wife’s parents went to the couple’s home to follow up on their marital problems, he killed both of them.

Another prisoner killed a young woman in August-September 2019 and subsequently, with the assistance of another individual, transported her body to the deserts near Robat Karim and set it on fire.

The report states that two other prisoners entered the home of an elderly man in Khordad 2020 with the intention of committing robbery and killed him during the robbery.

Another prisoner had been sentenced to death for the fatal shooting of a young man on March 14, 2024. During the investigation, he claimed that the victim had been harassing his sister.

title: Aida Ghaderi Arrested in Saqqez
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, Aida Ghaderi has been arrested.

According to the report, Aida Ghaderi was arrested at her home on Sunday, October 4, by Ministry of Intelligence agents without the presentation of a judicial warrant. She has also been denied access to an attorney, phone calls, and visits with her family.

Aida Ghaderi is a 20-year-old swimming instructor and athlete from Saqqez.

As of the time of this report, no information is available regarding her place of detention, the charges against her, or her current condition.

title: January 2026 Protests: Alireza Raisi Executed
content:
Based on information obtained by HRANA, Alireza Raisi was executed at dawn today, Monday, October 5, 2026, at Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan.

An informed source close to the Raisi family told HRANA about the hours leading up to the execution, saying that Mr. Raisi met with his family for the final time on Sunday, October 4. At the end of the visit, he refused to part from his family, and prison authorities and officers ultimately separated him from them by force. According to the source, members of his family also gathered outside Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan last night, seeking information about his situation.

Mr. Raisi’s death sentence was carried out at the same time as that of Alireza Sepahi, another defendant in the case.

Alireza Raisi had previously been sentenced to death along with several other defendants in the case known as the “Isfahan Alikhani Square” case. At the trial-court stage, 15 defendants in the case were sentenced to death. According to information provided by an attorney, the sentence of one defendant was overturned by a higher judicial authority, while the death sentences of the other 14 defendants were upheld.
snippet: Based on information obtained by HRANA, Alireza Raisi was executed at dawn today, Monday, October 5, 2026, at Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: World Teachers’ Day: At Least 47 Iranian Teachers Imprisoned, Detained, or in Exile
content:
World Teachers’ Day, observed annually on October 5, has been commemorated since 1994 and marks the anniversary of the adoption of the 1966 ILO/UNESCO Recommendation concerning the Status of Teachers. The document addresses, among other issues, teachers’ rights and responsibilities, conditions of employment, and standards for their working conditions and education.

Overview of Teachers’ Current Status

These 47 teachers are spread across 19 provinces in Iran. Razavi Khorasan has the highest number on the list, with eight individuals. It is followed by Fars and Khuzestan provinces, with five each; North Khorasan, with four; and Alborz and West Azerbaijan, with three each.

Kurdistan, Kermanshah, Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad, Markazi, Isfahan, and Tehran each have two individuals on the list, while Lorestan, Bushehr, Kerman, Zanjan, Gilan, Qazvin, and Ilam each have one.
snippet: World Teachers’ Day, observed annually on October 5, has been commemorated since 1994 and marks the anniversary of the adoption of the 1966 ILO/UNESCO Recommendation concerning the Status of Teachers.
